notes: Session 2. Closed B5-0649, on human approval to stop the two shipped census tools disagreeing about the same claim. A LIVE hermes run on B5-0631 made a theoretical disagreement observable: that run wrote its claim with a placeholder started_utc of 2026-09-27T00:00:00Z, so the claim's own age read 292 minutes against a 30-minute TTL; ledger-query.ps1 correctly called it LIVE off a 12-minute owner heartbeat, while run-queue.ps1 read started_utc ALONE and would have declared the claim abandoned and handed a task held by a working agent to a second claimant, which is the duplicate-delivery failure the whole claims protocol exists to prevent, one function call away. THE UNCOMFORTABLE PART: the B5-0597 lesson was already written down AND already implemented in ledger-query.ps1, and the second tool simply never received it, so the rule existed simultaneously as prose, as a working implementation, and as the opposite behaviour, with nothing reconciling them. A rule written down and implemented once is a rule one component follows, which is a latent duplicate-delivery bug wearing the costume of a convention. Fix: Test-LiveClaim now takes the NEWEST of the claim's own started_utc, falling back to claim file mtime, and the owner's heartbeat mtime, joined through Get-NormName COPIED VERBATIM from ledger-query.ps1, because the bug was never the started_utc logic but that the logic existed twice, and the fix for two drifting implementations is one implementation rather than two corrected copies. Heartbeat index rebuilt per call rather than cached, since one run may iterate many tasks over many minutes and a start-up cache would report a growing agent as silent. ONE DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE documented in the function: ledger-query prints UNKNOWN when no heartbeat matches the owner because it reports verdicts, whereas the runner's question is binary, so an owner who never wrote a heartbeat falls back to claim age, since not-live there would let one heartbeat-less claim block its task forever; when nothing can be determined the task is still not offered per 00_BOOT step 10. Verified the LIVE case first: runner now declines B5-0631 and offers B5-0633. Then seven synthetic cases in an isolated temp harness, all PASS, covering 9h-claim-no-heartbeat to FREE, the hermes case 9h-claim-plus-2min-heartbeat to TAKEN, 9h-claim-plus-8h-heartbeat to FREE, fresh-claim to TAKEN, corrupt claim never stolen, no claim to FREE, and future-dated treated as live for clock skew. HARNESS DEFECT DISCLOSED AND DISCARDED: the first synthetic run reported a near-uniform wrong answer because my timestamp format string had a typo making every timestamp unparseable so all cases fell back to claim-file mtime, and because a U+2028 separator was typed as literal text that is not a legal filename character; the corrected harness asserts up front that its generated timestamp parses, which is the check whose absence let a broken harness look authoritative. Also corrected the run-queue.ps1 header, which still described the superseded started_utc-only rule and cited 00_BOOT step 9 where reaping is step 10. The concurrent hermes run was never disturbed and was still alive at 19 minutes. Gates green: compile.bat Build successful, runner exit 0, no crash, no duplicate warning, B5-0631 correctly not offered. Reusable lesson: audit a convention by finding every place it is IMPLEMENTED and compare those places to each other, because a convention with N implementations has N-1 opportunities to disagree and the documentation counts for none of them.
